body:
## Summary

`detail::QdPutCallParityEngine::calculate()` — shared by both `QdPlusAmericanEngine` and `QdFpAmericanEngine` — checks only that the exercise type is American:

```cpp
QL_REQUIRE(arguments_.exercise->type() == Exercise::American,
           "not an American option");
```

It never inspects `AmericanExercise::payoffAtExpiry()`. Every other closed-form American engine explicitly rejects that flag, since their analytic formulas assume the standard immediate-early-exercise convention, not the payoff-deferred-to-expiry one:

- `BaroneAdesiWhaleyApproximationEngine`
- `BjerksundStenslandApproximationEngine`
- `JuQuadraticApproximationEngine`
- `McAmericanEngine` (via `EarlyExercise::payoffAtExpiry()`)

Without the same guard, QD+/QD-FP silently price a `payoffAtExpiry`-flagged American option as if it were a standard American option — a confidently wrong result with no indication anything is off, rather than the clean rejection every sibling closed-form engine gives.

## Fix

Added the same guard pattern used by the sibling engines (downcast to `AmericanExercise`, reject if `payoffAtExpiry()` is set), in the single shared `calculate()` so both `QdPlusAmericanEngine` and `QdFpAmericanEngine` are covered.

## Test

Added `testQdEnginesRejectPayoffAtExpiry` to `test-suite/americanoption.cpp`, covering both engines: confirms a plain American exercise still prices normally, and a `payoffAtExpiry`-flagged one throws. Without the fix, both engines compute a result instead of throwing; with the fix, both throw as expected. Full `AmericanOptionTests` suite (39 cases) passes with no regressions.

🤖 Co-worked with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)
title: Reject payoff-at-expiry exercise in Qd+/QdFp American engines
